refuted_main_function_hypothesis.verdict: Retained Pg3 denying immediate Black Kf4 is not established as the principal current choice value; the d16 named counter refutes that explanation here.
refuted_main_function_hypothesis.geometry_survives: After cxb4 original Pg3 is the sole f4 controller and Kf4 is illegal; after g4 Kf4 is legal. Kxe4 is legal after both choices.
refuted_main_function_hypothesis.counter: At d16 Black bxa3 is far stronger than Kf4 after g4; cxb4 remains advantageous when Black immediately captures original e4.

cxb4: Original White Pc3 captures original Black Pb4 immediately, preserving original White Pa3 as an exchange resource.
In the ...cxb4 arm, original Pa3 recaptures on b4; it is then a passed pawn. Black original Pc4 may advance c3 and be removed by original Pb2, with checks and subsequent passer losses retained.

In the ...Kxe4 arm, original Pe4 is deliberately lost. At d24 original Pc3 advances on b-file and is captured by Kxb7 while the White King captures original Black Pc4, Pc5 and Pa4. Original White Pb2 becomes a separate b-passer and promotes.
Original Pg3 advances later and is captured in these finite conversion lines. No permanent reserve or free gain is claimed.
g4: The move does not remove Black Pb4. Black bxa3 captures original White Pa3; original Pb2 can recapture that original Black Pb4 but lands a3 behind Black Pa4, while original Pc3 remains blocked by Black Pc4.
The returned stronger resistance includes Kxe4 and the loss of original Pg3 after g5. Black original Pf7 has a passed-pawn conversion path in returned d16 lines.
The current d24 named own line remains losing for White but does not itself reach a promotion; a d16 promotion event is not transplanted as a forced d24 event.
current_plan_function_and_prices.claim_level: The exact actions and finite state changes explain the tested current contrast. A single returned route is neither forced nor a whole root-cause proof.
